# Reservoir 1.7.0: shared-pool rent/return isolation

Predeclared for PR #3137. A1/A2: main `551d4d0825dca64b7143d6f18fc2b13baaf1fe0a`; B: `86f4b0e4b13d3a917d75b87121381bfce6424312`. Run the existing `pool` suite on one ubuntu-latest VM, sequential A1/B/A2. No product or fixture changes accompany this experiment.

Local exact-DLL inspection shows a changed `StripedObjectStore<T>.TryPop`: version 1.7.0 separates its first stripe attempt into `TryPopAt`, then calls `TryPopSlow` if needed. The first attempt retains the volatile read and compare-exchange of the stripe's fast item. This is a real change on the shared-pool path; its performance effect is not inferred from decompiled source. Dekaf's PendingRequestPool has shared capacity 256 and disables the thread-local fast path, so the existing rent/return benchmark directly exercises relevant storage and reset bookkeeping.

Separately, tracked thread-local clearing now retains LastTaken through WeakReference<T>. The ordinary rent body does not touch that weak reference unless clearing races its take. This observation does not identify a cause for previous steady-state producer maxima. The guarded reset path also preserves both reset and destroy failures through AggregateException; the Dekaf PendingRequestPool destroy callback only changes an Interlocked counter, so this double-failure path is not exercised by the normal benchmark.

The preceding published PR assessment is comment 5596144002. Earlier loaded measurements on older heads had 64 KiB tail losses and control drift. The #3142 experiment on run 34314789752 used a different candidate and cannot certify the dependency head: its ordinary pool A1/B/A2 means were 26.075/24.323/24.624 ns, with -5.57% control drift. No full loaded baseline has been accepted for the new #3137 head. This focused experiment tests the changed shared-pool cost; it does not substitute for fresh-head loaded CPU, actual-message latency or stability evidence, and is not another identical producer repetition.

Both products and the identical fixture are built and smoke-validated before timing. Each measured fresh process performs at least 20 seconds continuous workload warmup, then 30 one-second BDN warmups and 25 measured iterations, InProcessEmit, MemoryDiagnoser, DontRemove and affinity CPU 2. Keep the pool suite's existing tiered compilation/PGO/ReadyToRun settings enabled and record them. Verify actual elapsed warmup and runtime/JIT/GC/thread-pool time series; remaining startup transitions invalidate steady-state inference. Report mean-time and allocation results against both controls with uncertainty. The focused screen retains 3% mean loss/control drift and no allocation increase; require 0 B per rent/return operation. No applicable full-gate metric is waived by a narrower result.

Preserve exact product/harness SHAs, binary bindings, source archives, runner hardware/image, SDK/runtime and every raw BDN sample. The existing inventory covers host bindings; raw benchmark reports remain separately retained and must not be described as covered by that host-only inventory. Successful workflow execution remains INCONCLUSIVE pending review and the outstanding loaded scope.
